text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the prefix caching RFC — I prototyped a small shim that does lease-based backpressure on prefetches. sharing notes here for feedback.

maya: nice. what problem are you seeing that needs a shim vs. tuning eviction windows?

alex: mainly hotkey storms where prefetches pile up and evict useful entries while waiting for leases. tuning alone trades off tail latency vs hit-rate badly for mixed workloads.

sam: curious how the shim interacts with the existing lease acquisition flow. does it queue or reject prefetches?

alex: it implements a soft token bucket per-tenant + per-prefix-group. if a tenant exceeds tokens we return a controlled rejection to caller (so caller can fall back to cold read) and mark a short cooldown. avoids prefetch amplification.

chloe: controlled rejection sound risky for correctness (RAWrite). how do we ensure a read-after-write doesn't get stale?

alex: good call. allowance: we bypass token checks if request has recent write intent header (X-Recent-Write: ts). shim validates the header against local commit watermark. so RW gets high priority.

maya: watermark syncs are eventual — race window? if watermark lags a bit we could still return stale prefetched data.

alex: yes. plan: two-fold: 1) for write-affecting prefixes we short-circuit to authoritative fetch until our watermark confirmed, 2) instrument metrics for watermark lag per-shard and steer canary.

sam: what about fairness across tenants? token buckets per-tenant helps but hot prefixes within a tenant can still hog memory.

alex: we split budgeting: tenant budget + prefix-group subbudget. prefix groups are computed by hotness hash. groups can be demoted faster and have higher evaporative eviction weight.

chloe: eviction weight heuristics are sensitive. do you plan to rely on LRU variants or a scoring function?

alex: scoring function: score = alpha * recency + beta * access_count + gamma * resident_write_ratio - delta * prefetch_penalty. prefetch_penalty grows if item was brought in via prefetch and caused eviction within grace window.

tomas: re: prefetch_penalty — how do you detect "caused eviction" reliably in a distributed eviction path? could be tricky with delayed metrics.

alex: we add a causal marker: prefetch entries carry a tiny opaque token id. when eviction occurs we log the victim's token and the evictor's decision. offline analysis links tokens to recent evictions to tune penalty. runtime uses counters with bounded staleness.

infra-bot: deploy note: prototype build r12345 passed unit tests, staging smoke failing on high-concurrency kv bench (OOM).

maya: OOM expected until we wire the prefix-group demotion. can we short-circuit prefetch completely for the bench?

alex: yes, running variant with prefetch disabled now. early numbers: 30% higher tail latency but memory stable.

sam: how about correctness proof sketch? need to show no-read-after-write violations when prefetch+evict in-flight.

alex: sketch: invariants — (1) any write bumps per-prefix version; (2) reads include stable watermark or skip prefetch; (3) prefetch entries tagged with version when fetched; (4) on serving, if read's observed version > entry.version then entry is invalid and trigger authoritative fetch. proofs are informal but should cover races.

chloe: that sounds reasonable. we should add a failure-mode test: write -> immediate read on same prefix under heavy prefetch and forced eviction.

tomas: yes add property-based test that injects delays and verifies read sees latest. also add e2e perf with shard-local watermark skew.

maya: operational metrics we want: token saturation per-tenant, prefix-group demotion rate, prefetch_eviction_cause_ratio, watermark_lag_ms distribution, and RAWrite_miss_count.

alex: adding dashboards and alert thresholds. question for eng-ops: what SLA on watermark lag should we aim for? 50ms? 200ms?

sam: 200ms seems achievable at scale without huge sync traffic. 50ms might require synchronous replication. start with 200ms and iterate.

alex: plan: 1) land shim behind flag (prefetch_shim=true) with tenant and prefix buckets, 2) add token/metrics, 3) add write-bypass header and short-circuit on watermark, 4) test harness for RAWrite invariants + chaos injection, 5) staging canary disabled prefetch -> enabled shim -> observe metrics.

chloe: sounds good. small nit: ensure the bypass header can't be abused by clients — only internal writes should set it.

alex: agreed — only the write pipeline signs it with HMAC token validated by shard.

maya: thanks alex. can you drop a short design doc (1-2 pages) with diagrams and the scoring formula so we can RFC this change-set?

alex: will do. dropping a link to the proto after I clean it up. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC (flagged).

sam: ping me when the doc lands, I'll add chaos tests.

alex: thanks all.
